I have been farming in Quzhou County my whole life, and at 63 I know what this land can do. I have about 8 mu of flat, irrigated farmland. Last autumn I sowed winter wheat with an improved variety—this is the backbone of our village’s cropping system. Now that spring has arrived, my main job is to manage that wheat: irrigate it three or four times, top-dress with nitrogen, and spray for insects, weeds, and disease. After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize on the same plot without any tillage. No-tillage summer maize is what everyone here does; it saves fuel, labor, and precious time between the two crops. I expect roughly 500 kg per mu from each crop if the weather cooperates. I am not growing cotton this year—at my age, the dozen or so pesticide sprayings cotton demands are too hard on my back, and the wheat-maize double crop gives a steady, reliable income with machinery I can hire easily.
